title: Who ordered it, who wrote it, who drew it
lede: Titles follow the sources cited for each person. A later career is listed only where a source states it.

people.name: Sergio Zyman
people.role: Senior vice president and chief marketing officer, The Coca-Cola Company
people.text: Rejoined in August 1993 and introduced OK in New York the following April.[^1][^4] The Believer reports that he predicted a billion dollars in sales and 4% of the market.[^13]
people.later: Still listed as chief marketing officer in the 10-K filed in March 1996.[^3]

people.name: Brian Lanahan
people.role: Manager of special projects, Coca-Cola marketing
people.text: The company’s voice in Time’s 1994 report: “You have to first and foremost acknowledge that you are marketing.”[^6]

people.name: Peter Wegner
people.text: Wrote the manifesto and the “coincidences.” At 31, he defended the campaign in The Washington Post as a game.[^13][^8]
people.later: Left advertising; a multimedia artist in Berkeley, California, by 2014.[^13]

people.name: Todd Waterbury
people.role: Wegner’s collaborator on the campaign, Wieden & Kennedy
people.text: The campaign’s “visual mastermind,” in The Believer’s phrase, who hired the cartoonists.[^13]
people.later: Executive creative director at Target by 2014.[^13]

people.name: Daniel Clowes
people.text: Drew for the cans and gave his character Charles Manson’s eyes. He told The Believer the fee was more than he had made on his last five comics.[^13][^14]
people.later: Published Ghost World. In 2010 he recalled the soda as “gone in two months,” which is shorter than the record shows.[^13][^14]

people.name: Charles Burns
people.text: The other alternative cartoonist named in the 1994 coverage.[^8]

people.name: Tom Pirko
people.text: The consultant who described the taste on NPR and ranked taste below advertising, looks, availability and price.[^7]

people.name: Randy Donaldson
people.text: Announced the phase-out and gave the only sales figure.[^9]

people.name: Roberto Goizueta
people.text: Rehired Zyman in 1993, according to The Believer.[^13]
